questions.q: In this lab, why is the SLA Definition's Applies To condition set to `Priority is 1 Critical` instead of `Priority is 1 OR 2`?
options: ServiceNow does not allow an OR condition in Applies To
Widening it to Priority 2 would dilute a target the manager specifically meant for the most severe incidents
Priority 2 incidents are not eligible for any SLA
It has no effect on the SLA either way
questions.explain: Keeping Applies To narrow preserves the meaning of a target specifically meant for Priority 1 work.

questions.q: Why does this lab attach an '8-5 Weekdays' schedule to the 4-hour duration?
options: Schedules are required by the platform and have no real effect
So a Priority 1 opened late Friday doesn't falsely breach over the weekend, since the business only expects business-hours coverage for this target
To make the SLA run 24/7 regardless of when it's opened
To change the Applies To condition dynamically
questions.explain: The schedule makes the 4-hour target business-hours-aware, matching what the manager's requirement actually intends.

questions.q: Why does the lab's Pause condition deliberately exclude `hold_reason = Awaiting Vendor`?
options: Because Awaiting Vendor is not a valid Hold Reason value
Because vendor delays are inside the organization's control relative to the requirement, so that time should still count against the 4-hour target
Because the Pause condition can only reference one Hold Reason value at a time
Because Awaiting Vendor always triggers an automatic breach
questions.explain: The manager's requirement was specifically about not being penalized for caller wait time — the Pause condition is scoped to match only that, per the precise reading in the lab.

questions.q: In the lab's Step 5, why is Stop set to `state = Resolved` rather than `state = Closed`?
options: Resolved and Closed always happen at the same moment, so it doesn't matter
The clock should end when resolution evidence is recorded, not days later after caller confirmation closes the record
Closed is not a valid value to reference in a Stop condition
Stop conditions can only reference the Priority field
questions.explain: Measuring to Resolved captures the real resolution-time metric; waiting for Closed would inflate it with post-resolution confirmation delay.

questions.q: When the breach report shows Network Operations at 28% breach rate, what should you check next before concluding it's a staffing problem?
options: Nothing further is needed — a high breach rate always means understaffing
The group's average `business_percentage` consumed, even on tickets that didn't breach, to see how much real margin the team has
Whether the SLA Definition's Applies To condition includes Priority 2
Whether the `cmn_schedule` record has any holidays defined
questions.explain: Average percentage consumed distinguishes a real capacity gap from a team resolving on time but with very little margin — two different problems with two different fixes.
